newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cut-off yields to rise at Argentine Letes auction.
newsitem.headline: Cut-off yields to rise at Argentine Letes auction.

text.p: The cut-off yields at Argentina's auction Tuesday of 250 million pesos of 91-day Letes treasury bills and 500 million pesos of 364-day Letes are set to rise from the previous month's auction.

According to a Reuters survey of trader forecasts, the cut-off yield on the 91-day bills is set to be between 6.5 percent and seven percent. The average forecast was for a cut-off yield of 6.75 percent.
The cut-off yield on 91-day peso-denominated bills at last month's auction was 6.10 percent.
The current yield on Letes bills maturing on May 16 is 5.91 percent and on bills maturing on July 18 is 6.78 percent.

Forecasts on the 364-day bills, meanwhile, ranged from a low of 7.5 percent to a high of 8.5 percent. The average of the forecasts was 7.93 percent. Argentine Bonte treasury bonds maturing in December 1998 currently yield around 8.48 percent.

The 364-day bills will be the longest maturity Letes denominated in pesos that have been sold by the Economy Ministry since it started issuing Letes in April last year. Thus far, the longest maturities in pesos are six-month bills.

Traders said Tuesday's auction will be hit by the current poor market conditions caused by the market jitters surrounding the possible hike in U.S. rates when the Federal Open Market Committee meets March 25.
"Considering the current market climate, we expect higher rates than at the last auction," an analyst at a local brokerage house said.
